sections.title: Level 2 Strategy
sections.content: At Level 2, figures contain more than one element. Step 1: Identify all elements in the figure such as dots, arrows, stars, lines, or shading. Step 2: Observe how each element changes from A to B. Step 3: Note all transformations such as rotation, flip, or position change. Step 4: Apply the same rules to C and determine the correct D.

sections.title: Multi-Element Figure Analogy
sections.content: Some questions contain multiple symbols inside a box. Step 1: Observe the position and direction of each symbol. Step 2: Identify what changes occur from A to B. Step 3: Understand the transformation for each symbol separately. Step 4: Apply the same transformations to C. Example: A dot moves 90° clockwise, an arrow flips direction, and a star moves to the center.

sections.title: Complex Figure Classification
sections.content: In Level 2 classification, the rule may depend on multiple features. Step 1: Count the outer sides. Step 2: Observe intersecting lines inside the figure. Step 3: Identify the shading pattern. Step 4: Find the relationship among these features. Example: If the number of outer sides is two more than the number of inner lines, the same pattern should exist in the other figures.

sections.title: Mirror Image Concept
sections.content: In a mirror image, the figure is reversed from left to right. Step 1: Assume a vertical mirror. Step 2: The left side becomes the right side and the right side becomes the left. Step 3: The direction of symbols may change. Step 4: Choose the figure that matches the mirror transformation.

sections.title: Water Image Concept
sections.content: In a water image, the figure is reversed from top to bottom. Step 1: Imagine a horizontal reflection. Step 2: The top becomes the bottom. Step 3: The orientation flips downward. Step 4: Choose the option that correctly represents the water reflection.

sections.title: Identifying Mirror and Water Image in Analogy
sections.content: In many analogy questions, the transformation may involve mirror or water reflection. Step 1: Check whether the figure is reversed left to right. Step 2: Check whether it is reversed top to bottom. Step 3: Distinguish between rotation and reflection. Step 4: Apply the same rule to figure C.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Focusing on only one symbol instead of observing all elements. 2. Confusing mirror reflection with rotation. 3. Ignoring inner lines or shading patterns. 4. Failing to recognize multi-step transformations.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: At Level 2, figures usually involve multiple elements with combined transformations. In multi-element analogy, identify separate rules for each symbol. In classification, analyze relationships between shapes, lines, and shading. Correctly identifying mirror and water reflections is essential.

tricks.title: Element-by-Element Check
tricks.explanation: In multi-symbol boxes, analyze each symbol separately.
tricks.example: The dot moves, the arrow rotates, and the star shifts to the center.

tricks.title: Position Mapping Method
tricks.explanation: Mentally map positions such as top, bottom, left, and right.
tricks.example: A dot may move from the top position to the right position.

tricks.title: Side–Line Relationship
tricks.explanation: Observe the relationship between outer sides and inner lines.
tricks.example: A pentagon has 5 outer sides and 3 intersecting lines inside.

tricks.title: Shading Pattern Recognition
tricks.explanation: Shaded regions often shift clockwise or alternate positions.
tricks.example: The black region moves one corner forward in each step.

tricks.title: Mirror Shortcut
tricks.explanation: In mirror images, the left and right sides swap positions.
tricks.example: An arrow pointing left may appear pointing right.

tricks.title: Water Image Shortcut
tricks.explanation: In water images, the top and bottom positions swap.
tricks.example: An upward arrow appears downward in the water image.

tricks.title: Rotation vs Reflection
tricks.explanation: In rotation, orientation changes but sides do not swap positions.
tricks.example: An arrow rotates and changes direction.

tricks.title: Pattern Consistency Rule
tricks.explanation: In classification, identify the common pattern and find the figure that breaks the rule.
tricks.example: Four figures have the same sides-to-lines ratio, while one differs.
